content.text:
Recommend **A: one database definition of alias components, consumed by search and details**.

| Criterion | A: views | B: persisted groups | C: ingestion merging |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| One owner for grouping rules | 5 | 4 | 3 |
| Applies to existing records immediately | 5 | 3 | 1 |
| Preserves resolution identities and provenance | 5 | 5 | 2 |
| Small implementation and maintenance surface | 5 | 3 | 2 |
| Predictable query cost | 2 | 5 | 5 |

Use an ordinary view for direct undirected alias links and one recursive component membership view. Define matching once, using case and whitespace normalization consistently. Include canonical names in the matching vocabulary; the loader already stores canonical names among aliases, but fixtures and other writers need not do so.

Choose one deterministic representative funder per component. Both search paths must score existing indexed name candidates, map qualified candidates to components, select each component’s best match, and apply `LIMIT` **after** component deduplication. Preserve the winning match’s alias evidence when its name differs from the representative’s name.

Details should resolve any member ID to that same representative, collect aliases across all members, and aggregate funding entries once across component members. Member declaration links should use the representative too, so navigation and search expose the same identity.

Reject B for now because it adds derived state and a refresh obligation to a loader that currently owns resolved declaration persistence. Reject C because a search grouping requirement would alter the existing resolution identity model and require reprocessing artifacts.

**Major risk:** an ordinary recursive membership view can compute global transitive closure on every request, producing quadratic intermediate rows within large components. Verify the actual search and details plans against the frozen database before committing to A. If closure cost is unacceptable, retain the same grouping contract and use B’s atomic persisted projection.

The BBC, GB News, and Premier League cases should verify one result per component, identical details through every member ID, complete totals, transitive chains, and grouping before the search cap.

content.text:
Use explicit organization-family membership as a separate relationship from aliases.

Add two tables:

```sql
funder_families (
    family_key text PRIMARY KEY,
    canonical_name text NOT NULL
);

funder_family_names (
    family_key text REFERENCES funder_families,
    member_name text NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY (family_key, member_name)
);
```

Seed these reviewed names, matched using the existing case and whitespace normalization:

- **BBC:** BBC; BBC Contributor Payments; BBC Home Services; BBC Studios; BBC Studios Ltd; BBC Wales Cymru.
- **GB News:** GB News; GB News Limited; GB News Ltd.
- **Premier League:** Premier League; FA Premier League Ltd; The FA Premier League Ltd; The Premier League; Premier League International Holdings Ltd.

Define `funder_family_links` by joining matching funders within each family. Preserve `family_key`, both exact observed names, and an edge reason such as `organization_family`. Keep existing alias links and their direct alias evidence intact. A combined links view feeds the existing recursive component view; search and details continue sharing that component definition. Prefer the configured canonical family name for display.

Measured effect in the isolated database:

| Family | Funder rows | Current components | Result |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| BBC | 12 | 6 | 1 |
| GB News | 7 | 3 | 1 |
| Premier League | 7 | 4 | 1 |

The broader repeated-root substring rule produced 37 root labels with longer matches and incorrectly grouped Mauritius Labour Party with Labour Party. Explicit membership avoids that demonstrated collision while supporting future families through the same schema.

Create a new reversible migration pair. Its up migration creates and seeds family tables, adds family/combined link views, then replaces the component view to consume combined edges. Its down migration first restores the component view’s original alias-only definition, then drops combined links, family links, membership, and families in dependency order. Leave the already applied alias migration immutable. Verify both existing-data forward upgrade and down/up in the isolated database.
